_comment: Fishing and crabbing (Fisheries, scripts/sim/fisheries.gd). families: the seafood commodities (data/markets.json lists them too, with their prices), base $ a ton landed. species: what's caught, each in a family, by a gear (troll: lines trolled behind small boats; net: gillnets and purse seines; trawl: big dragged nets; trap: crab pots), its price a ton the family's times grade; a trophy is one giant fish that fills a small trolling boat's hold on its own. grounds: where each species is caught and in which months (1-12), how thick the catch is there (density), how much the ground holds (stock_t: fishing draws it down, it regrows over a year), its depth (inshore grounds take every boat; offshore ones the tier 2 and 3 boats; deep ones only the tier 3), and the months its seas are rough (crabbing and fishing there wears boats harder: the Bering Sea in winter).

red_king_crab.name: Red king crab
red_king_crab.fact: The biggest catch of the Bering Sea's crab fleet: a leg span up to 1.8 m, fished in Bristol Bay each October in the worst seas in the world.

blue_king_crab.name: Blue king crab
blue_king_crab.fact: Brown with blue highlights, it lives round the Pribilofs and St. Matthew Island and turns red when cooked.

golden_king_crab.name: Golden king crab
golden_king_crab.fact: The deepest of the king crabs, caught year round off the Aleutians in pots set 300 to 1,000 m down.

southern_king_crab.name: Southern king crab (centolla)
southern_king_crab.fact: Centolla: Patagonia's king crab, fished from Punta Arenas and Ushuaia in the Strait of Magellan and the Beagle Channel.

snow_crab.name: Snow crab (opilio)
snow_crab.fact: Opilio: long thin legs, sweet meat; fished in winter on the Bering Sea ice edge and each spring in the Gulf of St. Lawrence.

tanner_crab.name: Tanner crab (bairdi)
tanner_crab.fact: Bairdi, the bigger Tanner crab of the Bering Sea and the Gulf of Alaska.

red_snow_crab.name: Red snow crab (beni-zuwai)
red_snow_crab.fact: Beni-zuwai: a deep red snow crab from the Sea of Japan, caught in pots set 500 to 2,500 m down.

hair_crab.name: Horsehair crab (kegani)
hair_crab.fact: Kegani, the horsehair crab: covered in short bristles, the prized winter crab of Hokkaido.

dungeness_crab.name: Dungeness crab
dungeness_crab.fact: The Pacific coast's crab, from Alaska to California: only males over 16 cm may be kept, and the season opens in December.

blue_crab.name: Atlantic blue crab
blue_crab.fact: Callinectes sapidus, 'beautiful swimmer': Chesapeake Bay's and Louisiana's crab, eaten as soft-shells when it moults.

stone_crab.name: Florida stone crab
stone_crab.fact: Only a claw is taken and the crab put back to grow another: Florida's stone crab season runs from October to May.

brown_crab.name: Brown crab (edible crab)
brown_crab.fact: The edible crab of Britain, Ireland and Norway: a pie-crust edge to its shell and black-tipped claws.

jonah_crab.name: Jonah crab
jonah_crab.fact: Once a by-catch of New England's lobster pots, now a fishery of its own.

atlantic_rock_crab.name: Atlantic rock crab
atlantic_rock_crab.fact: A small Cancer crab of Atlantic Canada and New England, freckled purple.

pacific_rock_crab.name: Pacific rock crab
pacific_rock_crab.fact: The red rock crab of the Pacific coast, with heavy black-tipped claws.

spider_crab.name: European spider crab
spider_crab.fact: Centolla in Spain, araignée in France: a spiny spider crab whose spring migration fills the Breton and Galician pots.

velvet_crab.name: Velvet swimming crab
velvet_crab.fact: A fierce little swimming crab with red eyes and a velvety blue-black shell, shipped live from Scotland to Spain.

spanner_crab.name: Spanner crab
spanner_crab.fact: Shaped like a spanner: it buries itself in the sand off Queensland and is caught on flat dillies, not pots.

gazami_crab.name: Gazami crab
gazami_crab.fact: The Japanese blue crab, the world's biggest crab catch by weight: over 300,000 tonnes a year from the Yellow and East China Seas.

blue_swimmer_crab.name: Blue swimmer crab
blue_swimmer_crab.fact: The flower crab of Southeast Asia and Australia, picked by hand in Thai and Filipino villages.

mud_crab.name: Mud crab
mud_crab.fact: The mangrove crab of the Indo-Pacific, with claws that can crush a finger: caught in the Sundarbans, Queensland and East Africa.

red_crab.name: Deep-sea red crab
red_crab.fact: A deep-sea crab of the New England slope, caught in pots 600 m down along the canyons.

golden_crab.name: Golden deep-sea crab
golden_crab.fact: A deep-water crab of the slope off Florida and the Carolinas, caught 300 to 700 m down.

giant_crab.name: Tasmanian giant crab
giant_crab.fact: One of the heaviest crabs in the world, up to 13 kg: caught in deep pots on the edge of Bass Strait.

grounds.name: the Gulf of Mannar and Palk Bay
the waters off Cabo San Lucas
